say.text: Quick retrieval first. Without peeking, which set is the classic four components of TOF?

choices.label: VSD, overriding aorta, RVOT obstruction, right ventricular hypertrophy
VSD, overriding aorta, RVOT obstruction, left ventricular hypertrophy
ASD, VSD, RVOT obstruction, right ventricular hypertrophy

say.text: Right. A large, anteriorly malaligned VSD, an overriding aorta, infundibular RVOT obstruction and right ventricular hypertrophy.

say.text: Rung one: a hole. Which defect is one of the four components?
Think of the two pumping chambers. Which defect sits between them, with the aorta later sitting over it?
Yes: a large, anteriorly malaligned VSD.
An ASD is tempting: it is a septal hole that may accompany TOF. But it is not one of the four. The septal part is a large, anteriorly malaligned VSD.
A PDA is tempting: it too may accompany TOF. But it is not one of the four. The septal part is a large, anteriorly malaligned VSD.
Rung two: the great artery that leaves from above that hole. What is the component?
The component is about a vessel's position over the defect, not an extra channel. Which vessel carries blood to the body?
Yes: an overriding aorta.
A PDA is tempting because it may accompany TOF. But it is not one of the four. The aortic component is an overriding aorta.
Rung three: something obstructs blood leaving the right ventricle for the lungs. Which component is it?
Look at the name of the exit from the right ventricle. The obstruction sits just below the pulmonary valve.
Yes: infundibular (sub-pulmonary) RVOT obstruction.
An ASD is tempting: it may accompany TOF. But it is not one of the four. The obstruction component is infundibular (sub-pulmonary) RVOT obstruction.
A PDA is tempting: it may accompany TOF. But it is not one of the four. The obstruction component is infundibular (sub-pulmonary) RVOT obstruction.
Rung four: the right ventricle pumps against that obstruction at systemic pressures. Which ventricle's wall thickens?
Ask which ventricle faces the obstruction. The chamber under pressure is the one that hypertrophies.
Yes: right ventricular hypertrophy, secondary to chronic systemic pressures.
That completes the four: a large anteriorly malaligned VSD, an overriding aorta, infundibular RVOT obstruction and RVH.

say.text: Now a famous PYQ term. Pentalogy of Fallot is TOF plus which fifth lesion?
It is a septal hole, like the VSD, but between the two upper chambers.
Yes: pentalogy of Fallot is TOF plus an ASD; the term is old and seldom used now.
PYQs have expected this, and CDC confirms it.
A PDA is tempting because it may accompany TOF. But pentalogy of Fallot is TOF plus an atrial septal defect, an old term seldom used now.
